subject: [hw] V15: all 91 census mnemonics implemented; no UNDEF intersection
body:
Thanks for the V15 census (32166 instructions, 91 mnemonics). I checked the list one by one against my decoder: every mnemonic in it is implemented, including movw/movt/addw/subw/adr.w, mov.w/movt/mvn with modified immediates, and.w/and/orr/eor/bic/mvn/tst/cmn/teq, the shifted-register lsl/lsr/asr/ror/rrx forms, pkhbt, mla/mls/mul/umull/smulb*/smlalb*/smulwb/smull/umlal/smull, sdiv/udiv, ssat/usat, sbfx/ubfx/bfi/bfc, uxtb/uxth/uxtab/uxtah, rev.w, clz. So no V15 mnemonic used by the vendor set returns N2A32_UNDEF.

Two facts for FACTS.md, both [V] from llvm-mc 23.1.4 on this host:
1. The Thumb assembler canonicalises PKHTB with no shift to PKHBT with swapped operands: `pkhtb r0,r1,r2` assembles to EAC1 0002 = `pkhbt r0,r2,r1`. The encoding with PKHTB+shift_n==0 (EAC1 0022, type=10, imm5=0) is decoded by llvm-objdump as `pkhtb r0,r1,r2, asr #32`, i.e. it is a distinct encoding, not the no-shift form. V15 implements it as ASR #32.
2. ADC/SBC with a modified immediate (T32 encoding 11110 i 0 1010/1011 S Rn ...) are accepted by llvm-objdump but llvm-mc refuses to assemble them ("operand must be a register"), so the vendor set cannot contain them. V15 implements them; they are listed as untestable-by-assembly in my STATUS.
3. The 16-bit REV/REV16/REVSH/RBIT/CLZ family (0xFA9x/0xFABx) carries the source register in both first<3:0> and second<3:0> in all NDK-clang output (e.g. clz r0,r0 = FAB0 F080; 190 occurrences in libvcodecdrv). llvm-objdump reads first<3:0> as the source. V15 prefers second<3:0> and falls back to first<3:0> when it is 1111, so both encoders work.
